words.source_reading: חזן (ח ז ן; I could see no vowel points or rafe on any of the three letters)
words.image_evidence: In human376-complete-line.png the word after דער takes up about three glyph widths, not four. Its first glyph is the closed two-legged Rashi ח shape. It does not match the open hook-shaped Rashi ר found in the same line in דער, ספריכֿט and וואֶהרענד. Rashi ח is drawn as a ר-like stroke joined to a ו-like leg, which would explain a reading of רו. The middle glyph matches the ז in זאַגט in the same line, and the last is a long final ן. If the word were רוזן there should be a separate ו, and I can see no gap for one. חזן (Chasan) is also the standard Hebrew loanword in Judeo-German rubrics, and it fits 'spricht der …'.

words.source_reading: לייזע (ל י י ז ע; I could see no points)
words.image_evidence: The fourth glyph of the final word, just before the ע and the colon, has the same form as the Rashi ז in זאַגט and in the abbreviation א״ז״וו in the same line. It does not have the broad flat-topped Rashi ד shape of the ד in דער and וואֶהרענד. German 'leise' (quietly) is spelled לייזע. 'Leide' makes no sense here.

remaining_uncertainties: The crop is low resolution, with glyph bodies only about 20 px high. My reading rests on comparing glyph shapes within the same line, not on fine detail. I cannot rule out at this resolution a small point or rafe stroke on חזן or לייזע.

My readings overturn the two words the human marked tentative. I recommend the human confirm חזן and לייזע on a native-resolution crop before the candidate text is changed. Until then the human_uncertainties entries should stay.
'folgende' is printed without a final -s. Keep it as printed and do not normalize it to 'Folgendes'.
